ai.description: This skink reaches 15–20 cm. It features a brown dorsum with a distinct, dark-edged pale lateral stripe. Key identifiers include a smooth, shiny appearance and a slender, ribbon-like body shape.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Eurylepis taeniolata* is the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe bordered by dark edges along its flanks.
ai.habitat: The Ribbon-sided Skink inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Indian subcontinent, typically found among leaf litter at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ribbon-sided Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eurylepis taeniolata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, roughly from April to July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eurylepis taeniolata* is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Punjab, typically at low to moderate elevations.
